facts.text: In the middle of the 1800s, the narrow old streets of central London were badly crowded with horse-drawn traffic.
London's mainline railway stations brought large numbers of travelers into the city, and moving between these stations added to the crowding on the streets.
Charles Pearson pushed the idea of running trains under the ground after getting stuck in heavy street traffic himself.
The first line was built by the cut-and-cover method: workers dug a large trench, laid the railway inside it, and then covered it over.
Builders preferred to dig the trench under an existing road, so that fewer houses had to be knocked down.
Cut and cover was a rough but fast way to build, and it caused years of disruption in central London.
The Metropolitan Railway, the first underground railway in the world, had a formal opening on 9 January 1863 and opened to the public on 10 January 1863.
About 650 important guests attended the formal opening of the line, which included a banquet at Farringdon station.
The first line ran between Paddington (then called Bishop's Road) and Farringdon Street.
The first line had only seven stops, and all seven are still in use today.
On the first day of public service, around 40,000 passengers rode the new railway.
Passengers sat in first-class, second-class, or third-class compartments, and the carriages were pulled by steam engines.
Smoke, soot, and steam from the engines filled the tunnels from the very first day, which made the ride unpleasant and added to the confusion on opening day.
A poster of rules for passengers did not allow smoking or riding on the roof of the carriages.
Dogs were not allowed to travel in the carriages with passengers; they were carried separately, and their owners had to pay for this.
In 1890, the City and South London Railway opened as the world's first deep-level electric tube railway.
In 1961, steam locomotives stopped pulling passenger trains on London's transport network.
In 2023, Transport for London marked 160 years of public service on the line; by 2026 the first underground railway had been open for more than 160 years.
facts.note: 衍生數字：2023 年為 160 週年

facts.text: In 2023, the London Underground network had 11 lines, 272 stations, and about 250 miles of track.

notes: 首日乘客數各來源不一（約 30,000～40,000），文章只用 TfL 與英國國家檔案館都寫的「約 40,000」。
